sanskrit: te nivṛttā mahākāyāḥ śrutvāṅgadavacas tadā naiṣṭhikīṃ buddhim āsthāya sarve saṃgrāmakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Those mighty-bodied ones, having heard the words of Aṅgada, turned back and assumed a resolute mind, all eager for battle.

sanskrit: samudīritavīryās te samāropitavikramāḥ paryavasthāpitā vākyair aṅgadena valīmukhāḥ
english: Their valor stirred up and their courage heightened, the monkeys were rallied by the words of Aṅgada.

sanskrit: prayātāś ca gatā harṣaṃ maraṇe kṛtaniścayāḥ cakruḥ sutumulaṃ yuddhaṃ vānarās tyaktajīvitāḥ
english: Setting forth, the monkeys became joyful, having resolved on death; they fought a most tumultuous battle, having cast aside all concern for their lives.

sanskrit: atha vṛkṣān mahākāyāḥ sānūni sumahānti ca vānarās tūrṇam udyamya kumbhakarṇam abhidravan
english: Then those mighty-bodied monkeys, quickly lifting up trees and great mountain peaks, rushed toward Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇaḥ saṃkruddho gadām udyamya vīryavān ardayan sumahākāyaḥ samantād vyākṣipad ripūn
english: That valiant Kumbhakarṇa, exceedingly wrathful, lifting up his mace, of tremendous body, crushed and scattered the enemies on every side.

sanskrit: śatāni sapta cāṣṭau ca sahasrāṇi ca vānarāḥ prakīrṇāḥ śerate bhūmau kumbhakarṇena pothitāḥ
english: Seven hundred, eight hundred, thousands of monkeys lay scattered on the ground, crushed by Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśāṣṭau ca daśa ca viṃśat triṃśat tathaiva ca parikṣipya ca bāhubhyāṃ khādan viparidhāvati bhakṣayan bhṛśasaṃkruddho garuḍaḥ pannagān iva
english: Sixteen, eight, ten, twenty, thirty at a time — seizing them with his arms and devouring them, he ran about eating them; exceedingly enraged, like Garuḍa among serpents.

sanskrit: hanūmāñ śailaśṛṅgāṇi vṛkṣāṃś ca vividhān bahūn vavarṣa kumbhakarṇasya śirasy ambaram āsthitaḥ
english: Hanūmān, stationed in the sky, rained down mountain peaks and many kinds of trees upon the head of Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: tāni parvataśṛṅgāṇi śūlena tu bibheda ha babhañja vṛkṣavarṣaṃ ca kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
english: Kumbhakarṇa of great strength shattered those mountain peaks with his spear and broke apart the shower of trees.

sanskrit: tato harīṇāṃ tad anīkam ugraṃ dudrāva śūlaṃ niśitaṃ pragṛhya tasthau tato 'syāpatataḥ purastān mahīdharāgraṃ hanumān pragṛhya
english: Then that fierce army of monkeys fled; but Hanūmān stood before him as he charged, grasping a mountain peak.

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇaṃ kupito jaghāna vegena śailottamabhīmakāyam sa cukṣubhe tena tadābhibūto medārdragātro rudhirāvasiktaḥ
english: Enraged, he struck Kumbhakarṇa of terrible frame swiftly with the finest of mountains; Kumbhakarṇa was shaken thereby and overcome, his body dripping with fat and drenched in blood.

sanskrit: sa śūlam āvidhya taḍitprakāśaṃ giriṃ yathā prajvalitāgraśṛṅgam bāhvantare mārutim ājaghāna guho 'calaṃ krauñcam ivograśaktyā
english: He whirled his spear, blazing like lightning, and struck the son of the Wind between his arms, as Guha once struck the Krauñca mountain with his fierce lance.

sanskrit: sa śūlanirbhinna mahābhujāntaraḥ pravihvalaḥ śoṇitam udvaman mukhāt nanāda bhīmaṃ hanumān mahāhave yugāntameghastanitasvanopamam
english: Hanūmān, his great chest pierced by the spear, staggered and vomiting blood from his mouth, let out a terrible roar in the great battle, like the sound of thunder at the end of an age.

sanskrit: tato vineduḥ sahasā prahṛṣṭā rakṣogaṇās taṃ vyathitaṃ samīkṣya plavaṃgamās tu vyathitā bhayārtāḥ pradudruvuḥ saṃyati kumbhakarṇāt
english: Thereupon the hosts of rākṣasas suddenly roared with delight seeing him afflicted; the monkeys, distressed and overwhelmed with fear, fled from Kumbhakarṇa in the battle.

sanskrit: nīlaś cikṣepa śailāgraṃ kumbhakarṇāya dhīmate tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya muṣṭinābhijaghāna ha
english: Nīla hurled a mountain peak at the wise Kumbhakarṇa; seeing it coming toward him, Kumbhakarṇa struck it with his fist.

sanskrit: muṣṭiprahārābhihataṃ tac chailāgraṃ vyaśīryata savisphuliṅgaṃ sajvālaṃ nipapāta mahītale
english: That mountain peak, struck by the blow of his fist, shattered and fell to the earth with sparks and flames.

sanskrit: ṛṣabhaḥ śarabho nīlo gavākṣo gandhamādanaḥ pañcavānaraśārdūlāḥ kumbhakarṇam upādravan
english: Ṛṣabha, Śarabha, Nīla, Gavākṣa, and Gandhamādana — these five foremost monkeys rushed upon Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: śailair vṛkṣais talaiḥ pādair muṣṭibhiś ca mahābalāḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahākāyaṃ sarvato 'bhinijaghnire
english: Those mighty ones struck the great-bodied Kumbhakarṇa from all sides with rocks, trees, palms, feet, and fists.

sanskrit: sparśān iva prahārāṃs tān vedayāno na vivyathe ṛṣabhaṃ tu mahāvegaṃ bāhubhyāṃ pariṣasvaje
english: Feeling those blows as if mere touches, he did not flinch; but the swift Ṛṣabha he clasped in his arms.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇabhujābhyāṃ tu pīḍito vānararṣabhaḥ nipapātarṣabho bhīmaḥ pramukhāgataśoṇitaḥ
english: That terrible bull among monkeys, crushed by Kumbhakarṇa's arms, fell, with blood flowing from his mouth.

sanskrit: muṣṭinā śarabhaṃ hatvā jānunā nīlam āhave ājaghāna gavākṣaṃ ca talenendraripus tadā
english: The enemy of Indra then struck Śarabha with his fist, Nīla with his knee in battle, and Gavākṣa with his palm.

sanskrit: dattapraharavyathitā mumuhuḥ śoṇitokṣitāḥ nipetus te tu medinyāṃ nikṛttā iva kiṃśukāḥ
english: Tormented by the blows given to them, drenched in blood, they fainted and fell to earth like felled kiṃśuka trees.

sanskrit: teṣu vānaramukhyeṣu patiteṣu mahātmasu vānarāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi kumbhakarṇaṃ pradudruvuḥ
english: When those great-souled monkey chiefs had fallen, thousands of monkeys fled from Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ śailam iva śailābhāḥ sarve tu plavagarṣabhāḥ samāruhya samutpatya dadaṃśuś ca mahābalāḥ
english: All those mighty bull-monkeys, themselves resembling mountains, leapt upon him as upon a mountain, climbed him and bit him.

sanskrit: taṃ nakhair daśanaiś cāpi muṣṭibhir jānubhis tathā kumbhakarṇaṃ mahākāyaṃ te jaghnuḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: Those bull-monkeys struck the great-bodied Kumbhakarṇa with nails, teeth, fists, and knees.

sanskrit: sa vānarasahasrais tair ācitaḥ parvatopamaḥ rarāja rākṣasavyāghro girir ātmaruhair iva
english: Covered by those thousands of monkeys, that tiger among rākṣasas, who resembled a mountain, shone like a hill covered with its own trees.

sanskrit: bāhubhyāṃ vānarān sarvān pragṛhya sa mahābalaḥ bhakṣayām āsa saṃkruddho garuḍaḥ pannagān iva
english: Seizing all the monkeys with his arms, that mighty one devoured them, enraged, like Garuḍa devouring serpents.

sanskrit: prakṣiptāḥ kumbhakarṇena vaktre pātālasaṃnibhe nāsā puṭābhyāṃ nirjagmuḥ karṇābhyāṃ caiva vānarāḥ
english: Monkeys thrown by Kumbhakarṇa into his mouth, which resembled the underworld, emerged through his nostrils and his ears.

sanskrit: bhakṣayan bhṛśasaṃkruddho harīn parvatasaṃnibhaḥ babhañja vānarān sarvān saṃkruddho rākṣasottamaḥ
english: Devouring the monkeys with extreme fury, that foremost of rākṣasas, who resembled a mountain, smashed all the monkeys, exceedingly enraged.

sanskrit: māṃsaśoṇitasaṃkledāṃ bhūmiṃ kurvan sa rākṣasaḥ cacāra harisainyeṣu kālāgnir iva mūrchitaḥ
english: Making the ground a mire of flesh and blood, that rākṣasa moved through the monkey army like the fire of universal dissolution blazing intensely.

sanskrit: vajrahasto yathā śakraḥ pāśahasto ivāntakaḥ śūlahasto babhau tasmin kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
english: The mighty Kumbhakarṇa in that battle shone forth, spear in hand, as Śakra with the thunderbolt in his hand, as Antaka with his noose in hand.

sanskrit: yathā śuṣkāṇy araṇyāni grīṣme dahati pāvakaḥ tathā vānarasainyāni kumbhakarṇo vinirdahat
english: As fire burns dry forests in summer, so Kumbhakarṇa consumed the monkey armies.

sanskrit: tatas te vadhyamānās tu hatayūthā vināyakāḥ vānarā bhayasaṃvignā vinedur visvaraṃ bhṛśam
english: Then those monkeys, being slaughtered, their herd-leaders slain, trembling with fear, cried out discordantly and piteously.

sanskrit: anekaśo vadhyamānāḥ kumbhakarṇena vānarāḥ rāghavaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmur vyathitāḥ khinnacetasaḥ
english: The monkeys, being slaughtered repeatedly by Kumbhakarṇa, afflicted and downcast in heart, sought refuge with Rāghava.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam utpapāta tadā vīraḥ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ
english: Seeing that mighty Kumbhakarṇa charging forward, the heroic Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, leapt up.

sanskrit: sa parvatāgram utkṣipya samāvidhya mahākapiḥ abhidudrāva vegena kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam
english: That great monkey, lifting a mountain peak and whirling it about, rushed swiftly at the mighty Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya kumbhakarṇaḥ plavaṃgamam tasthau vivṛtasarvāṅgo vānarendrasya saṃmukhaḥ
english: Seeing that monkey rushing upon him, Kumbhakarṇa stood with all his limbs exposed, facing the king of the monkeys.

sanskrit: kapiśoṇitadigdhāṅgaṃ bhakṣayantaṃ mahākapīn kumbhakarṇaṃ sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sugrīvo vākyam abravīt
english: Seeing Kumbhakarṇa standing there with his body smeared with the blood of monkeys, devouring great monkeys, Sugrīva spoke.

sanskrit: pātitāś ca tvayā vīrāḥ kṛtaṃ karma suduṣkaram bhakṣitāni ca sainyāni prāptaṃ te paramaṃ yaśaḥ
english: "Warriors have been felled by you; a most difficult feat has been accomplished; armies have been devoured; supreme glory has been won by you.

sanskrit: tyaja tad vānarānīkaṃ prākṛtaiḥ kiṃ kariṣyasi sahasvaikaṃ nipātaṃ me parvatasyāsya rākṣasa
english: Abandon that monkey army — what use have you for these ordinary ones? Bear one blow from me, rākṣasa, with this mountain."

sanskrit: tad vākyaṃ harirājasya sattvadhairyasamanvitam śrutvā rākṣasaśārdūlaḥ kumbhakarṇo 'bravīd vacaḥ
english: Hearing that speech of the monkey king, imbued with courage and steadfastness, Kumbhakarṇa, tiger among rākṣasas, replied.

sanskrit: prajāpates tu pautras tvaṃ tathaivarkṣarajaḥsutaḥ śrutapauruṣasaṃpannas tasmād garjasi vānara
english: "You are indeed the grandson of Prajāpati and the son of Ṛkṣaraja; you are endowed with famed valor — that is why you roar so, monkey."

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇasya vaco niśamya vyāvidhya śailaṃ sahasā mumoca tenājaghānorasi kumbhakarṇaṃ śailena vajrāśanisaṃnibhena
english: Hearing Kumbhakarṇa's words, he suddenly whirled the mountain and released it; with that mountain, resembling a thunderbolt or lightning, he struck Kumbhakarṇa in the chest.

sanskrit: tac chailaśṛṅgaṃ sahasā vikīrṇaṃ bhujāntare tasya tadā viśāle tato viṣeduḥ sahasā plavaṃgamā rakṣogaṇāś cāpi mudā vineduḥ
english: That mountain peak was instantly shattered against his broad chest; thereupon the monkeys were suddenly downcast while the hosts of rākṣasas cried out with joy.

sanskrit: sa śailaśṛṅgābhihataś cukopa nanāda kopāc ca vivṛtya vaktram vyāvidhya śūlaṃ ca taḍitprakāśaṃ cikṣepa haryṛkṣapater vadhāya
english: Struck by the mountain peak, he became enraged and roared in his fury, opening wide his mouth; whirling his lightning-bright spear, he hurled it to slay the lord of the monkeys.

sanskrit: tat kumbhakarṇasya bhujapraviddhaṃ śūlaṃ śitaṃ kāñcanadāmajuṣṭam kṣipraṃ samutpatya nigṛhya dorbhyāṃ babhañja vegena suto 'nilasya
english: That sharp spear hurled by Kumbhakarṇa's arms, adorned with a golden garland, was quickly leapt upon by the son of Anila, who caught and swiftly broke it with his arms.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ bhārasahasrasya śūlaṃ kālāyasaṃ mahat babhañja janaum āropya prahṛṣṭaḥ plavagarṣabhaḥ
english: That great spear of dark iron, made to bear a thousand loads, was broken by that bull among monkeys, who placed his knee upon it, delighted.

sanskrit: sa tat tadā bhagnam avekṣya śūlaṃ cukopa rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā utpāṭya laṅkāmalayāt sa śṛṅgaṃ jaghāna sugrīvam upetya tena
english: Seeing his spear broken, the great-souled lord of the rākṣasas became enraged; uprooting a peak from Laṅkā's Malaya range, he approached and struck Sugrīva with it.

sanskrit: sa śailaśṛṅgābhihato visaṃjñaḥ papāta bhūmau yudhi vānarendraḥ taṃ prekṣya bhūmau patitaṃ visaṃjñaṃ neduḥ prahṛṣṭā yudhi yātudhānāḥ
english: The king of the monkeys, struck by the mountain peak, fell insensible to the ground in battle; seeing him fallen insensible to the ground, the rākṣasas roared with delight in battle.

sanskrit: tam abhyupetyādbhutaghoravīryaṃ sa kumbhakarṇo yudhi vānarendram jahāra sugrīvam abhipragṛhya yathānilo megham atipracaṇḍaḥ
english: Approaching that king of monkeys with his wondrously terrible might, Kumbhakarṇa seized and carried off Sugrīva in battle, even as the exceedingly violent wind carries off a cloud.

sanskrit: sa taṃ mahāmeghanikāśarūpam utpāṭya gacchan yudhi kumbhakarṇaḥ rarāja merupratimānarūpo merur yathātyucchritaghoraśṛṅgaḥ
english: Kumbhakarṇa, tearing him away and moving in battle, of a form comparable to Meru, shone forth with the one who resembled a great cloud — like Meru with its terribly high peaks.

sanskrit: tataḥ samutpāṭya jagāma vīraḥ saṃstūyamāno yudhi rākṣasendraiḥ śṛṇvan ninādaṃ tridaśālayānāṃ plavaṃgarājagrahavismitānām
english: Then the hero tore him away and went, being praised by the lords of rākṣasas in battle, hearing the cries of the gods in their heaven, who were astonished at the capture of the monkey king.

sanskrit: tatas tam ādāya tadā sa mene harīndram indropamam asmin hṛte sarvam idaṃ hṛtaṃ syāt sarāghavaṃ sainyam itīndraśatruḥ
english: Then taking him, the enemy of Indra thought regarding that Indra-like lord of monkeys: "With this one taken captive, the entire army together with Rāghava would be undone."

sanskrit: vidrutāṃ vāhinīṃ dṛṣṭvā vānarāṇāṃ tatas tataḥ kumbhakarṇena sugrīvaṃ gṛhītaṃ cāpi vānaram
english: Seeing the monkey army fleeing in every direction and Sugrīva the monkey seized by Kumbhakarṇa,

sanskrit: hanūmāṃś cintayām āsa matimān mārutātmajaḥ evaṃ gṛhīte sugrīve kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayā bhavet
english: the wise Hanūmān, son of the Wind, began to reflect: "With Sugrīva seized in this manner, what is it that I should do?"

sanskrit: yad vai nyāyyaṃ mayā kartuṃ tat kariṣyāmi sarvathā bhūtvā parvatasaṃkāśo nāśayiṣyāmi rākṣasaṃ
english: "Whatever is right for me to do, that I shall do by every means; assuming a form like a mountain, I shall destroy the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: mayā hate saṃyati kumbhakarṇe mahābale muṣṭiviśīrṇadehe vimocite vānarapārthive ca bhavantu hṛṣṭāḥ pravagāḥ samagrāḥ
english: "When the mighty Kumbhakarṇa has been slain by me in battle, his body crushed by my fists, and the monkey king freed, let all the monkeys be glad."

sanskrit: atha vā svayam apy eṣa mokṣaṃ prāpsyati pārthivaḥ gṛhīto 'yaṃ yadi bhavet tridaśaiḥ sāsuroragaiḥ
english: "Or else the king himself will gain release — even if he were seized by the gods together with asuras and serpents,

sanskrit: manye na tāvad ātmānaṃ budhyate vānarādhipaḥ śailaprahārābhihataḥ kumbhakarṇena saṃyuge
english: "I think the lord of monkeys does not yet regain his senses, having been struck by the mountain blow from Kumbhakarṇa in battle.

sanskrit: ayaṃ muhūrtāt sugrīvo labdhasaṃjño mahāhave ātmano vānarāṇāṃ ca yat pathyaṃ tat kariṣyati
english: "In a moment Sugrīva, having regained consciousness in the great battle, will do what is beneficial for himself and for the monkeys.

sanskrit: mayā tu mokṣitasyāsya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ aprītaś ca bhavet kaṣṭā kīrtināśaś ca śāśvataḥ
english: "But if I were to rescue the great-souled Sugrīva, both his displeasure would result and the permanent loss of his glory would be grievous.

sanskrit: tasmān muhūrtaṃ kāṅkṣiṣye vikramaṃ pārthivasya naḥ bhinnaṃ ca vānarānīkaṃ tāvad āśvāsayāmy aham
english: "Therefore I shall wait a moment for the valor of our king; in the meantime I shall reassure the scattered monkey army."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ cintayitvā tu hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ bhūyaḥ saṃstambhayām āsa vānarāṇāṃ mahācamūm
english: Having thus reflected, Hanūmān, son of the Wind, once again steadied the great army of monkeys.

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇo 'tha viveśa laṅkāṃ sphurantam ādāya mahāhariṃ tam vimānacaryāgṛhagopurasthaiḥ puṣpāgryavarṣair avakīryamāṇaḥ
english: Then Kumbhakarṇa entered Laṅkā carrying that great monkey who was writhing and struggling, showered with the finest flowers by those standing in the aerial cars, mansions, and gatehouses.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa saṃjñām upalabhya kṛcchrād balīyasas tasya bhujāntarasthaḥ avekṣamāṇaḥ purarājamārgaṃ vicintayām āsa muhur mahātmā
english: Then the great-souled one, held between the arms of the stronger foe, with difficulty regaining his senses, and surveying the royal roads of the city, reflected again and again.

sanskrit: evaṃ gṛhītena kathaṃ nu nāma śakyaṃ mayā saṃprati kartum adya tathā kariṣyāmi yathā harīṇāṃ bhaviṣyatīṣṭaṃ ca hitaṃ ca kāryam
english: "Being seized in this way, what can I possibly do now? I shall act in such a way that what is desired and beneficial for the monkeys will be accomplished."

sanskrit: tataḥ karāgraiḥ sahasā sametya rājā harīṇām amarendraśatroḥ nakhaiś ca karṇau daśanaiś ca nāsāṃ dadaṃśa pārśveṣu ca kumbhakarṇam
english: Then the king of the monkeys, suddenly striking with the tips of his fingers, bit with his nails into the ears and with his teeth into the nose of the enemy of Indra, and tore at his flanks with his claws.

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇau hṛtakarṇanāso vidāritas tena vimarditaś ca roṣābhibhūtaḥ kṣatajārdragātraḥ sugrīvam āvidhya pipeṣa bhūmau
english: Kumbhakarṇa, his ears and nose torn away, ripped and pounded by him, overwhelmed with rage, his body wet with blood, hurled Sugrīva down and crushed him to the ground.

sanskrit: sa bhūtale bhīmabalābhipiṣṭaḥ surāribhis tair abhihanyamānaḥ jagāma khaṃ vegavad abhyupetya punaś ca rāmeṇa samājagāma
english: Crushed on the ground by those enemies of the gods with their terrible strength, beaten by them, he swiftly took to the sky and returned to Rāma.

sanskrit: karṇanāsā vihīnasya kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ rarāja śoṇitotsikto giriḥ prasravaṇair iva
english: The mighty Kumbhakarṇa, deprived of his ears and nose, drenched in blood, shone forth like a mountain with its streams.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa puryāḥ sahasā mahātmā niṣkramya tad vānarasainyam ugram babhakṣa rakṣo yudhi kumbhakarṇaḥ prajā yugāntāgnir iva pradīptaḥ
english: Then the great-souled Kumbhakarṇa suddenly sallied from the city and devoured that fierce monkey army in battle, blazing like the fire of universal destruction.

sanskrit: bubhukṣitaḥ śoṇitamāṃsagṛdhnuḥ praviśya tad vānarasainyam ugram cakhāda rakṣāṃsi harīn piśācān ṛkṣāṃś ca mohād yudhi kumbhakarṇaḥ
english: Hungry and greedy for blood and flesh, Kumbhakarṇa penetrated that fierce monkey army and in his frenzy devoured in battle rākṣasas, monkeys, piśācas, and bears alike.

sanskrit: ekaṃ dvau trīn bahūn kruddho vānarān saha rākṣasaiḥ samādāyaikahastena pracikṣepa tvaran mukhe
english: Enraged, he seized one, two, three, many — monkeys along with rākṣasas in one hand — and swiftly flung them into his mouth.

sanskrit: saṃprasravaṃs tadā medaḥ śoṇitaṃ ca mahābalaḥ vadhyamāno nagendrāgrair bhakṣayām āsa vānarān te bhakṣyamāṇā harayo rāmaṃ jagmus tadā gatim
english: Dripping with fat and blood, that mighty one, even while being struck by the tips of great mountains, devoured the monkeys; and those monkeys who were being devoured then fled to Rāma for refuge.

sanskrit: tasmin kāle sumitrāyāḥ putraḥ parabalārdanaḥ cakāra lakṣmaṇaḥ kruddho yuddhaṃ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: At that time the son of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, crusher of enemy forces, conqueror of enemy cities, waged battle in anger.

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇasya śarāñ śarīre sapta vīryavān nicakhānādade cānyān visasarja ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: That valiant Lakṣmaṇa drove seven arrows deep into Kumbhakarṇa's body, took up other arrows, and released them.

sanskrit: atikramya ca saumitriṃ kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ rāmam evābhidudrāva dārayann iva medinīm
english: Passing by Saumitri, the mighty Kumbhakarṇa charged straight at Rāma alone, as if splitting the earth.

sanskrit: atha dāśarathī rāmo raudram astraṃ prayojayan kumbhakarṇasya hṛdaye sasarja niśitāñ śarān
english: Then Rāma, son of Daśaratha, employing the dread weapon, shot sharp arrows into Kumbhakarṇa's heart.

sanskrit: tasya rāmeṇa viddhasya sahasābhipradhāvataḥ aṅgāramiśrāḥ kruddhasya mukhān niścerur arciṣaḥ
english: From the mouth of the one pierced by Rāma and rushing forward, flames mixed with embers streamed forth in his rage.

sanskrit: tasyorasi nimagnāś ca śarā barhiṇavāsasaḥ hastāc cāsya paribhraṣṭā papātorvyāṃ mahāgadā
english: The peacock-plumed arrows sank into his chest, and the great mace fell from his hand to the earth.

sanskrit: sa nirāyudham ātmānaṃ yadā mene mahābalaḥ muṣṭibhyāṃ cāraṇābhyāṃ ca cakāra kadanaṃ mahat
english: When that mighty one realized he was weaponless, he wrought great havoc with his two fists and with his feet.

sanskrit: sa bāṇair atividdhāṅgaḥ kṣatajena samukṣitaḥ rudhiraṃ parisusrāva giriḥ prasravaṇān iva
english: His body pierced all over with arrows, soaked with gore, he oozed blood like a mountain with its springs.

sanskrit: sa tīvreṇa ca kopena rudhireṇa ca mūrchitaḥ vānarān rākṣasān ṛkṣān khādan viparidhāvati
english: Maddened by intense rage and by blood, he ran about devouring monkeys, rākṣasas, and bears.

sanskrit: tasmin kāle sa dharmātmā lakṣmaṇo rāmam abravīt kumbhakarṇavadhe yukto yogān parimṛśan bahūn
english: At that time the righteous Lakṣmaṇa, engaged in the slaying of Kumbhakarṇa and considering many strategies, spoke to Rāma.

sanskrit: naivāyaṃ vānarān rājan na vijānāti rākṣasān mattaḥ śoṇitagandhena svān parāṃś caiva khādati
english: "O king, he no longer distinguishes between monkeys and rākṣasas; maddened by the smell of blood he devours friend and foe alike.

sanskrit: sādhv enam adhirohantu sarvato vānararṣabhāḥ yūthapāś ca yathāmukhyās tiṣṭhantv asya samantataḥ
english: "It is best that all the bull-monkeys climb upon him from every side, and let the herd-leaders, all the chiefs, stand around him.

sanskrit: apy ayaṃ durmatiḥ kāle gurubhāraprapīḍitaḥ prapatan rākṣaso bhūmau nānyān hanyāt plavaṃgamān
english: "Perhaps this foolish rākṣasa, pressed down by the heavy burden in due time and falling to the earth, will not then slay any more monkeys."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājaputrasya dhīmataḥ te samāruruhur hṛṣṭāḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: Hearing that speech of the wise prince, those monkeys gladly climbed upon Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇas tu saṃkruddhaḥ samārūḍhaḥ plavaṃgamaiḥ vyadhūnayat tān vegena duṣṭahastīva hastipān
english: Kumbhakarṇa, exceedingly enraged, with the monkeys clambering all over him, shook them off with speed, as a rogue elephant shakes off its mahouts.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā nirdhūtān rāmo ruṣṭo 'yam iti rākṣasaḥ samutpapāta vegena dhanur uttamam ādade
english: Seeing them shaken off, Rāma thought "this rākṣasa is enraged" and leapt up swiftly, taking up his finest bow.

sanskrit: sa cāpam ādāya bhujaṃgakalpaṃ dṛḍhajyam ugraṃ tapanīyacitram harīn samāśvāsya samutpapāta rāmo nibaddhottamatūṇabāṇaḥ
english: Taking up that bow, resembling a great serpent, with a firm string, fierce, adorned with gold, and having reassured the monkeys, Rāma leapt up with his best quiver of arrows strapped on.

sanskrit: sa vānaragaṇais tais tu vṛtaḥ paramadurjayaḥ lakṣmaṇānucaro rāmaḥ saṃpratasthe mahābalaḥ
english: That mighty Rāma, supremely difficult to conquer, surrounded by those bands of monkeys and attended by Lakṣmaṇa, set forth.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ kirīṭinam ariṃdamam śoṇitāplutasarvāṅgaṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam
english: He beheld the great-souled, diadem-wearing, enemy-subduing, mighty Kumbhakarṇa, his entire body drenched in blood.

sanskrit: sarvān samabhidhāvantaṃ yathāruṣṭaṃ diśā gajam mārgamāṇaṃ harīn kruddhaṃ rākṣasaiḥ parivāritam
english: He saw him charging all directions like a maddened elephant, stalking the monkeys in fury, surrounded by rākṣasas.

sanskrit: vindhyamandarasaṃkāśaṃ kāñcanāṅgadabhūṣaṇam sravantaṃ rudhiraṃ vaktrād varṣamegham ivotthitam
english: He resembled the Vindhya or Mandara mountain, adorned with golden armlets, blood streaming from his mouth like a rain-cloud risen up.

sanskrit: jihvayā parilihyantaṃ śoṇitaṃ śoṇitokṣitam mṛdnantaṃ vānarānīkaṃ kālāntakayamopamam
english: He licked the blood with his tongue, drenched in blood, crushing the monkey army, comparable to Yama at the end of an age.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaśreṣṭhaṃ pradīptānalavarcasaṃ visphārayām āsa tadā kārmukaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Seeing that foremost of rākṣasas, blazing with the splendor of a lit fire, that bull among men then twanged his bow.

sanskrit: sa tasya cāpanirghoṣāt kupito nairṛtarṣabhaḥ amṛṣyamāṇas taṃ ghoṣam abhidudrāva rāghavam
english: At the sound of his bow, that bull among rākṣasas became enraged, unable to endure that sound, and rushed at Rāghava.

sanskrit: tatas tu vātoddhatameghakalpaṃ bhujaṃgarājottamabhogabāhum tam āpatantaṃ dharaṇīdharābham uvāca rāmo yudhi kumbhakarṇam
english: Then Rāma spoke in battle to Kumbhakarṇa who charged like a cloud swept up by the wind, with arms like the coils of a great serpent king, and resembling a mountain.

sanskrit: āgaccha rakṣo'dhipamā viṣādam avasthito 'haṃ pragṛhītacāpaḥ avehi māṃ śakrasapatna rāmam ayaṃ muhūrtād bhavitā vicetāḥ
english: "Come, lord of rākṣasas, do not despair — I stand here, bow in hand. Know me as Rāma, rival of Śakra; in a moment you will be senseless."

sanskrit: rāmo 'yam iti vijñāya jahāsa vikṛtasvanam pātayann iva sarveṣāṃ hṛdayāni vanaukasām
english: Recognizing this as Rāma, he laughed with a hideous sound, as if making the hearts of all the forest-dwellers sink.

sanskrit: prahasya vikṛtaṃ bhīmaṃ sa meghasvanitopamam kumbhakarṇo mahātejā rāghavaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Laughing hideously and fearfully with a sound like thunder, the mighty-splendored Kumbhakarṇa spoke to Rāghava.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ virādho vijñeyo na kabandhaḥ kharo na ca na vālī na ca mārīcaḥ kumbhakarṇo 'ham āgataḥ
english: "I am not to be thought of as Virādha, nor as Kabandha, nor as Khara, nor as Vālin, nor as Mārīca — I am Kumbhakarṇa who has come.

sanskrit: paśya me mudgaraṃ ghoraṃ sarvakālāyasaṃ mahat anena nirjitā devā dānavāś ca mayā purā
english: "Behold my terrible mace of solid iron — with this I formerly conquered the gods and dānavas.

sanskrit: vikarṇanāsa iti māṃ nāvajñātuṃ tvam arhasi svalpāpi hi na me pīḍā karṇanāsāvināśanāt
english: "You should not despise me as one without ears and nose — even the loss of ears and nose gives me no pain worth mentioning.

sanskrit: darśayekṣvākuśārdūla vīryaṃ gātreṣu me laghu tatas tvāṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi dṛṣṭapauruṣavikramam
english: "Show your valor upon my body freely, O tiger of the Ikṣvākus; then I shall devour you once your heroic prowess has been displayed."

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇasya vaco niśamya rāmaḥ supuṅkhān visasarja bāṇān tair āhato vajrasamapravegair na cukṣubhe na vyathate surāriḥ
english: Hearing Kumbhakarṇa's words, Rāma released well-feathered arrows; struck by them, equal in speed to the thunderbolt, the enemy of the gods neither wavered nor was pained.

sanskrit: yaiḥ sāyakaiḥ sālavarā nikṛttā vālī hato vānarapuṃgavaś ca te kumbhakarṇasya tadā śarīraṃ vajropamā na vyathayāṃ pracakruḥ
english: Those arrows by which the finest śāla trees were severed, by which Vālin the bull among monkeys was slain — those thunderbolt-like arrows then could not distress Kumbhakarṇa's body.

sanskrit: sa vāridhārā iva sāyakāṃs tān pibañ śarīreṇa mahendraśatruḥ jaghāna rāmasya śarapravegaṃ vyāvidhya taṃ mudgaram ugravegam
english: The enemy of great Indra, drinking up those arrows with his body as if they were streams of water, countered Rāma's arrow-force by whirling and hurling that mace with terrible speed.

sanskrit: tatas tu rakṣaḥ kṣatajānuliptaṃ vitrāsanaṃ devamahācamūnām vyāvidhya taṃ mudgaram ugravegaṃ vidrāvayām āsa camūṃ harīṇām
english: Then that rākṣasa, smeared with blood, terror of the great divine armies, whirling that mace of terrible velocity, put the monkey army to flight.

sanskrit: vāyavyam ādāya tato varāstraṃ rāmaḥ pracikṣepa niśācarāya samudgaraṃ tena jahāra bāhuṃ sa kṛttabāhus tumulaṃ nanāda
english: Then Rāma took up the excellent Vāyavya weapon and shot it at the night-ranger; with it he severed the arm together with the mace; with his arm cut off, he let out a tumultuous roar.

sanskrit: sa tasya bāhur giriśṛṅgakalpaḥ samudgaro rāghavabāṇakṛttaḥ papāta tasmin harirājasainye jaghāna tāṃ vānaravāhinīṃ ca
english: That arm of his, like a mountain peak, together with the mace, severed by Rāghava's arrow, fell upon the monkey-king's army and struck that monkey force.

sanskrit: te vānarā bhagnahatāvaśeṣāḥ paryantam āśritya tadā viṣaṇṇāḥ pravepitāṅgā dadṛśuḥ sughoraṃ narendrarakṣo'dhipasaṃnipātam
english: Those monkeys, the remnant of the broken and slain, retreating to the flanks, downcast and trembling-limbed, beheld that most terrible clash of the king of men and the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇo 'stranikṛttabāhur mahān nikṛttāgra ivācalendraḥ utpāṭayām āsa kareṇa vṛkṣaṃ tato 'bhidudrāva raṇe narendram
english: Kumbhakarṇa, that great one with his arm cut off by the weapon, like a great mountain with its peak severed, uprooted a tree with his remaining hand and then charged at the king of men in battle.

sanskrit: taṃ tasya bāhuṃ saha sālavṛkṣaṃ samudyataṃ pannagabhogakalpam aindrāstrayuktena jahāra rāmo bāṇena jāmbūnadacitritena
english: Rāma severed that arm of his raised along with the śāla tree, resembling a serpent's coil, with an arrow charged with the Aindra weapon, decorated with gold.

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇasya bhujo nikṛttaḥ papāta bhūmau girisaṃnikāśaḥ viveṣṭamāno nijaghāna vṛkṣāñ śailāñ śilāvānararākṣasāṃś ca
english: That arm of Kumbhakarṇa, cut off, fell to the earth, resembling a mountain; writhing, it struck trees, hills, rocks, monkeys, and rākṣasas.

sanskrit: taṃ chinnabāhuṃ samavekṣya rāmaḥ samāpatantaṃ sahasā nadantam dvāv ardhacandrau niśitau pragṛhya ciccheda pādau yudhi rākṣasasya
english: Seeing him with both arms severed, charging suddenly and roaring, Rāma seized two sharp crescent-shaped arrows and cut off the feet of the rākṣasa in battle.

sanskrit: nikṛttabāhur vinikṛttapādo vidārya vaktraṃ vaḍavāmukhābham dudrāva rāmaṃ sahasābhigarjan rāhur yathā candram ivāntarikṣe
english: His arms cut off and his feet severed, gaping open his mouth which resembled the mare's fire at ocean's end, he rushed at Rāma with a sudden roar, as Rāhu rushes at the moon in the sky.

sanskrit: apūrayat tasya mukhaṃ śitāgrai rāmaḥ śarair hemapinaddhapuṅkhaiḥ sa pūrṇavaktro na śaśāka vaktuṃ cukūja kṛcchreṇa mumoha cāpi
english: Rāma filled his mouth with arrows of sharp points, with gold-bound shafts; with his mouth full he could not speak, he gurgled with difficulty and even fainted.

sanskrit: athādade sūryamarīcikalpaṃ sa brahmadaṇḍāntakakālakalpam ariṣṭam aindraṃ niśitaṃ supuṅkhaṃ rāmaḥ śaraṃ mārutatulyavegam
english: Then Rāma took up that arrow comparable to the rays of the sun, comparable to the rod of Brahmā and the end of time, unerring, charged with Aindra energy, sharp, well-feathered, equal in speed to the wind.

sanskrit: taṃ vajrajāmbūnadacārupuṅkhaṃ pradīptasūryajvalanaprakāśam mahendravajrāśanitulyavegaṃ rāmaḥ pracikṣepa niśācarāya
english: Rāma shot at the night-ranger that arrow with beautiful shaft of thunderbolt and gold, with the brilliance of the blazing sun, equal in speed to the bolt of great Indra.

sanskrit: sa sāyako rāghavabāhucodito diśaḥ svabhāsā daśa saṃprakāśayan vidhūmavaiśvānaradīptadarśano jagāma śakrāśanitulyavikramaḥ
english: That arrow, impelled by Rāghava's arm, illuminating the ten directions with its own light, appearing blazing like a smokeless fire, went forth equal in might to the thunderbolt of Śakra.

sanskrit: sa tan mahāparvatakūṭasaṃnibhaṃ vivṛttadaṃṣṭraṃ calacārukuṇḍalam cakarta rakṣo'dhipateḥ śiras tadā yathaiva vṛtrasya purā puraṃdaraḥ
english: It severed the head of the lord of rākṣasas — that head resembling a great mountain peak, with bared tusks and swaying lovely earrings — even as Puraṃdara once severed the head of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tad rāmabāṇābhihataṃ papāta rakṣaḥśiraḥ parvatasaṃnikāśam babhañja caryāgṛhagopurāṇi prākāram uccaṃ tam apātayac ca
english: That rākṣasa's head, struck by Rāma's arrow, fell, mountain-like, smashing the promenades, mansions, and gatehouses, and toppling the high rampart.

sanskrit: tac cātikāyaṃ himavatprakāśaṃ rakṣas tadā toyanidhau papāta grāhān mahāmīnacayān bhujaṃgamān mamarda bhūmiṃ ca tathā viveśa
english: That enormous rākṣasa body, resembling the Himālaya, fell into the ocean, crushed crocodiles, great masses of fish, and serpents, and submerged into the earth as well.

sanskrit: tasmir hate brāhmaṇadevaśatrau mahābale saṃyati kumbhakarṇe cacāla bhūr bhūmidharāś ca sarve harṣāc ca devās tumulaṃ praṇeduḥ
english: When the mighty Kumbhakarṇa, enemy of the Brāhmaṇas and gods, had been slain in battle, the earth and all its mountains shook, and the gods cried out in tumultuous joy.

sanskrit: tatas tu devarṣimaharṣipannagāḥ surāś ca bhūtāni suparṇaguhyakāḥ sayakṣagandharvagaṇā nabhogatāḥ praharṣitā rāma parākrameṇa
english: Then the divine sages, great sages, serpents, gods, spirits, Suparṇas, Guhyakas, bands of Yakṣas and Gandharvas dwelling in the sky were filled with joy at Rāma's valor.

sanskrit: praharṣam īyur bahavas tu vānarāḥ prabuddhapadmapratimair ivānanaiḥ apūjayan rāghavam iṣṭabhāginaṃ hate ripau bhīmabale durāsade
english: Many monkeys were filled with delight, their faces like blooming lotuses, and they praised Rāghava, the beloved, with the enemy of terrible strength and unapproachable prowess slain.

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇaṃ surasainyamardanaṃ mahatsu yuddheṣv aparājitaśramam nananda hatvā bharatāgrajo raṇe mahāsuraṃ vṛtram ivāmarādhipaḥ
english: Having slain in battle Kumbhakarṇa, crusher of divine armies, unwearied and unconquered in great battles, Bharata's elder brother rejoiced, as the lord of the immortals rejoiced upon slaying the great asura Vṛtra.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghaveṇa mahātmanā rākṣasā rākṣasendrāya rāvaṇāya nyavedayan
english: Having seen Kumbhakarṇa slain by the great-souled Rāghava, the rākṣasas reported it to Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: śrutvā vinihataṃ saṃkhye kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam rāvaṇaḥ śokasaṃtapto mumoha ca papāta ca
english: Hearing that the mighty Kumbhakarṇa had been slain in battle, Rāvaṇa, consumed by grief, fainted and fell.

sanskrit: pitṛvyaṃ nihataṃ śrutvā devāntakanarāntakau triśirāś cātikāyaś ca ruruduḥ śokapīḍitāḥ
english: Hearing that their paternal uncle had been slain, Devāntaka, Narāntaka, Triśiras, and Atikāya wept, afflicted with grief.

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ nihataṃ śrutvā rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā mahodaramahāpārśvau śokākrāntau babhūvatuḥ
english: Hearing that their brother had been slain by the tireless Rāma, Mahodara and Mahāpārśva were overcome by grief.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛcchrāt samāsādya saṃjñāṃ rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ kumbhakarṇavadhād dīno vilalāpa sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Then that foremost of rākṣasas, with great difficulty regaining his senses, Rāvaṇa, broken by the death of Kumbhakarṇa, lamented.

sanskrit: hā vīra ripudarpaghna kumbhakarṇa mahābala śatrusainyaṃ pratāpyaikaḥ kva māṃ saṃtyajya gacchasi
english: "Ah, hero, crusher of enemy pride, mighty Kumbhakarṇa — having alone scorched the enemy army, where do you go, abandoning me?

sanskrit: idānīṃ khalv ahaṃ nāsmi yasya me patito bhujaḥ dakṣiṇo yaṃ samāśritya na bibhemi surāsurān
english: "Now indeed I am as nothing, for my right arm has fallen — that arm on which I relied and feared not gods nor asuras.

sanskrit: katham evaṃvidho vīro devadānavadarpahā kālāgnipratimo hy adya rāghaveṇa raṇe hataḥ
english: "How could such a hero, crusher of the pride of gods and dānavas, like the fire of time, be slain today by Rāghava in battle?

sanskrit: yasya te vajraniṣpeṣo na kuryād vyasanaṃ sadā sa kathaṃ rāmabāṇārtaḥ prasupto 'si mahītale
english: "You for whom the crushing blow of the thunderbolt never caused suffering — how are you now laid low by Rāma's arrows, sleeping on the earth?

sanskrit: ete devagaṇāḥ sārdham ṛṣibhir gagane sthitāḥ nihataṃ tvāṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā ninadanti praharṣitāḥ
english: "These hosts of gods standing in the sky together with seers, seeing you slain in battle, cry out overjoyed.

sanskrit: dhruvam adyaiva saṃhṛṣṭā labdhalakṣyāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ ārokṣyantīha durgāṇi laṅkādvārāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: "Surely today the monkeys, their goal achieved and overjoyed, will climb the fortifications and scale all the gates of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: rājyena nāsti me kāryaṃ kiṃ kariṣyāmi sītayā kumbhakarṇavihīnasya jīvite nāsti me ratiḥ
english: "I have no need of the kingdom, what shall I do with Sītā — without Kumbhakarṇa I find no pleasure in life.

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ bhrātṛhantāraṃ na hanmi yudhi rāghavam nanu me maraṇaṃ śreyo na cedaṃ vyarthajīvitam
english: "If I do not slay Rāghava, the slayer of my brother, in battle, then surely death is better for me; otherwise this life is meaningless.

sanskrit: adyaiva taṃ gamiṣyāmi deśaṃ yatrānujo mama na hi bhrātṝn samutsṛjya kṣaṇaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: "Today I shall go to that place where my younger brother is; for I cannot bear to live even a moment having abandoned my brothers.

sanskrit: devā hi māṃ hasiṣyanti dṛṣṭvā pūrvāpakāriṇam katham indraṃ jayiṣyāmi kumbhakarṇahate tvayi
english: "The gods will mock me, seeing one who has previously offended them. How shall I conquer Indra, with you, Kumbhakarṇa, slain?

sanskrit: tad idaṃ mām anuprāptaṃ vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śubham yad ajñānān mayā tasya na gṛhītaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: "That good counsel of Vibhīṣaṇa has now come back to me — which I, out of ignorance, did not accept from that great-souled one.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇavaco yāvat kumbhakarṇaprahastayoḥ vināśo 'yaṃ samutpanno māṃ vrīḍayati dāruṇaḥ
english: "This destruction that has arisen for both Kumbhakarṇa and Prahasta, because of my not heeding Vibhīṣaṇa's counsel, fills me with bitter shame.

sanskrit: tasyāyaṃ karmaṇaḥ prāto vipāko mama śokadaḥ yan mayā dhārmikaḥ śrīmān sa nirasto vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: "This is the fruit, come to me in due course and causing grief, of that deed — when I expelled the righteous and glorious Vibhīṣaṇa."

sanskrit: iti bahuvidham ākulāntarātmā kṛpaṇam atīva vilapya kumbhakarṇam nyapatad atha daśānano bhṛśārtas tam anujam indraripuṃ hataṃ viditvā
english: Having thus lamented most pitifully in many ways, his inner soul in turmoil, knowing his younger brother the enemy of Indra to be slain, the ten-faced Rāvaṇa fell down, sorely afflicted.

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapamānasya rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ śrutvā śokābhitaptasya triśirā vākyam abravīt
english: As the evil-souled Rāvaṇa lamented thus, scorched by grief, Triśiras heard him and spoke.

sanskrit: evam eva mahāvīryo hato nas tāta madhyamaḥ na tu satpuruṣā rājan vilapanti yathā bhavān
english: "Our middle uncle of great valor has indeed been slain, father; but righteous men, O king, do not lament as you do.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ tribhuvaṇasyāpi paryāptas tvam asi prabho sa kasmāt prākṛta iva śokasyātmānam īdṛśam
english: "Surely you, O lord, are sufficient even for the three worlds; why then do you subject yourself to grief like an ordinary man?

sanskrit: brahmadattāsti te śaktiḥ kavacaḥ sāyako dhanuḥ sahasrakharasaṃyukto ratho meghasamasvanaḥ
english: "You have the lance granted by Brahmā, a coat of armor, arrows, a bow, a chariot yoked to a thousand asses and roaring like thunder.

sanskrit: tvayāsakṛd viśastreṇa viśastā devadānavāḥ sa sarvāyudhasaṃpanno rāghavaṃ śāstum arhasi
english: "By you the gods and dānavas have been repeatedly slaughtered even without weapons; so fully equipped with every weapon, you are fit to chastise Rāghava.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tiṣṭha mahārājanirgamiṣyāmy ahaṃ raṇam uddhariṣyāmi te śatrūn garuḍaḥ pannagān iha
english: "Please remain, O great king; I shall go forth to battle and shall pull out your enemies here like Garuḍa pulling out serpents.

sanskrit: śambaro devarājena narako viṣṇunā yathā tathādya śayitā rāmo mayā yudhi nipātitaḥ
english: "As Śambara was laid low by the king of gods and Naraka by Viṣṇu, so today shall Rāma be laid low and slain by me in battle."

sanskrit: śrutvā triśiraso vākyaṃ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ punar jātam ivātmānaṃ manyate kālacoditaḥ
english: Hearing Triśiras's words, Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, impelled by fate, felt as if he had been born again.

sanskrit: śrutvā triśiraso vākyaṃ devāntakanarāntakau atikāyaś ca tejasvī babhūvur yuddhaharṣitāḥ
english: Hearing Triśiras's words, Devāntaka, Narāntaka, and the mighty Atikāya became filled with battle-joy.

sanskrit: tato 'ham aham ity evaṃ garjanto nairṛtarṣabhāḥ rāvaṇasya sutā vīrāḥ śakratulyaparākramāḥ
english: Then, each roaring "I, I" — the sons of Rāvaṇa, heroes among rākṣasas, equal in valor to Śakra,

sanskrit: antarikṣacarāḥ sarve sarve māyā viśāradāḥ sarve tridaśadarpaghnāḥ sarve ca raṇadurmadāḥ
english: All of them moving through the sky, all skilled in illusion, all crushers of divine pride, all maddened by battle,

sanskrit: sarve 'strabalasaṃpannāḥ sarve vistīrṇa kīrtayaḥ sarve samaram āsādya na śrūyante sma nirjitāḥ
english: All endowed with the power of weapons, all of wide-spread fame, all having engaged in battle — never had they been heard of as defeated,

sanskrit: sarve 'straviduṣo vīrāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ sarve pravarajijñānāḥ sarve labdhavarās tathā
english: All heroes versed in arms, all skilled in warfare, all eager to excel, all having obtained boons —

sanskrit: sa tais tathā bhāskaratulyavarcasaiḥ sutair vṛtaḥ śatrubalapramardanaiḥ rarāja rājā maghavān yathāmarair vṛto mahādānavadarpanāśanaiḥ
english: Surrounded thus by those sons of solar radiance, crushers of enemy forces, the king shone forth as Maghavan shines surrounded by the immortals, destroyers of the pride of great dānavas.

sanskrit: sa putrān saṃpariṣvajya bhūṣayitvā ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ āśīrbhiś ca praśastābhiḥ preṣayām āsa saṃyuge
english: He embraced his sons, adorned them with ornaments, and sent them forth to battle with auspicious blessings.

sanskrit: mahodaramahāpārśvau bhrātarau cāpi rāvaṇaḥ rakṣaṇārthaṃ kumārāṇāṃ preṣayām āsa saṃyuge
english: Rāvaṇa also sent his brothers Mahodara and Mahāpārśva to battle for the protection of the princes.

sanskrit: te 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ rāvaṇaṃ ripurāvaṇam kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ caiva mahākāyāḥ pratasthire
english: They saluted the great-souled Rāvaṇa, terror of enemies, performed circumambulation, and those great-bodied ones set forth.

sanskrit: sarvauṣadhībhir gandhaiś ca samālabhya mahābalāḥ nirjagmur nairṛtaśreṣṭhāḥ ṣaḍ ete yuddhakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Anointed with all medicinal herbs and perfumes, these six foremost rākṣasas of great strength set out, eager for battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ sudarśanaṃ nāma nīlajīmūtasaṃnibham airāvatakule jātam āruroha mahodaraḥ
english: Then Mahodara mounted an elephant named Sudarśana, blue-cloud-like, born of the lineage of Airāvata.

sanskrit: sarvāyudhasamāyuktaṃ tūṇībhiś ca svalaṃkṛtam rarāja gajam āsthāya savitevāstamūrdhani
english: Equipped with all weapons and well adorned with quivers, he shone mounted on the elephant like the sun on the mountaintop at setting.

sanskrit: hayottamasamāyuktaṃ sarvāyudhasamākulam āruroha rathaśreṣṭhaṃ triśirā rāvaṇātmajaḥ
english: Triśiras, son of Rāvaṇa, mounted the finest chariot, yoked with best horses and full of all weapons.

sanskrit: triśirā ratham āsthāya virarāja dhanurdharaḥ savidyudulkaḥ sajvālaḥ sendracāpa ivāmbudaḥ
english: Triśiras, bow in hand, mounted on his chariot, shone forth like a storm cloud with lightning, meteor, flames, and the rainbow of Indra.

sanskrit: tribhiḥ kirīṭais triśirāḥ śuśubhe sa rathottame himavān iva śailendras tribhiḥ kāñcanaparvataiḥ
english: Triśiras with his three diadems gleamed on that finest chariot like the Himālaya, king of mountains, with three golden peaks.

sanskrit: atikāyo 'pi tejasvī rākṣasendrasutas tadā āruroha rathaśreṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām
english: The mighty Atikāya, son of the lord of rākṣasas, best of all archers, also mounted the finest chariot.

sanskrit: sucakrākṣaṃ susaṃyuktaṃ sānukarṣaṃ sakūbaram tūṇībāṇāsanair dīptaṃ prāsāsi parighākulam
english: That chariot was perfectly wheeled and well-equipped, with a strong axle and yoke, blazing with quivers, bows, and arrows, crowded with spears, swords, and clubs.

sanskrit: sa kāñcanavicitreṇa kirīṭena virājatā bhūṣaṇaiś ca babhau meruḥ prabhābhir iva bhāsvaraḥ
english: With his shining golden diadem and ornaments, he blazed forth like Mount Meru luminous with its own light.

sanskrit: sa rarāja rathe tasmin rājasūnur mahābalaḥ vṛto nairṛtaśārdūlair vajrapāṇir ivāmaraiḥ
english: That mighty son of the king shone on that chariot, surrounded by tiger-like rākṣasas, like Vajrapāṇi surrounded by the immortals.

sanskrit: hayam uccaiḥśravaḥ prakhyaṃ śvetaṃ kanakabhūṣaṇam manojavaṃ mahākāyam āruroha narāntakaḥ
english: Narāntaka mounted a white horse resembling Uccaiḥśravas, adorned with gold, swift as thought, of great frame.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā prāsam uklābhaṃ virarāja narāntakaḥ śaktim ādāya tejasvī guhaḥ śatruṣv ivāhave
english: Grasping a gleaming lance, Narāntaka shone forth, that mighty one taking his śakti, like Guha among enemies in battle.

sanskrit: devāntakaḥ samādāya parighaṃ vajrabhūṣaṇam parigṛhya giriṃ dorbhyāṃ vapur viṣṇor viḍambayan
english: Devāntaka took up his iron club adorned with thunderbolt-marks, grasped a mountain in his arms, mimicking the form of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: mahāpārśvo mahātejā gadām ādāya vīryavān virarāja gadāpāṇiḥ kubera iva saṃyuge
english: The greatly splendid and valiant Mahāpārśva, mace in hand, shone forth in battle like Kubera with his mace.

sanskrit: te pratasthur mahātmāno balair apratimair vṛtāḥ surā ivāmarāvatyāṃ balair apratimair vṛtāḥ
english: Those great-souled ones set forth, surrounded by matchless forces, like gods in Amarāvatī surrounded by matchless forces.

sanskrit: tān gajaiś ca turaṃgaiś ca rathaiś cāmbudanisvanaiḥ anujagmur mahātmāno rākṣasāḥ pravarāyudhāḥ
english: Those great-souled rākṣasas bearing the finest weapons followed them with elephants, horses, and chariots thundering like rain-clouds.

sanskrit: te virejur mahātmāno kumārāḥ sūryavarcasaḥ kirīṭinaḥ śriyā juṣṭā grahā dīptā ivāmbare
english: Those great-souled princes, of solar radiance, diademed, endowed with glory, blazed like brilliant planets in the sky.

sanskrit: pragṛhītā babhau teṣāṃ chatrāṇām āvaliḥ sitā śāradābhrapratīkāśāṃ haṃsāvalir ivāmbare
english: The white row of parasols held aloft over them shone like a row of autumn clouds, like a line of swans in the sky.

sanskrit: maraṇaṃ vāpi niścitya śatrūṇāṃ vā parājayam iti kṛtvā matiṃ vīrā nirjagmuḥ saṃyugārthinaḥ
english: Having resolved on death or on the defeat of enemies, those heroes set forth with their minds made up, eager for battle.

sanskrit: jagarjuś ca praṇeduś ca cikṣipuś cāpi sāyakān jahṛṣuś ca mahātmāno niryānto yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: They roared, they shouted, they shot arrows, and those great-souled ones maddened by battle rejoiced as they marched out.

sanskrit: kṣveḍitāsphoṭaninadaiḥ saṃcacāleva medinī rakṣasāṃ siṃhanādaiś ca pusphoṭeva tadāmbaram
english: With the hissing, snapping, and thunderous sounds the earth seemed to quake; with the lion-roars of the rākṣasas the sky seemed to burst.

sanskrit: te 'bhiniṣkramya muditā rākṣasendrā mahābalāḥ dadṛśur vānarānīkaṃ samudyataśilānagam
english: Those mighty lords of rākṣasas, joyful, sallying forth, beheld the monkey army with its rocks and trees raised aloft.

sanskrit: harayo 'pi mahātmāno dadṛśur nairṛtaṃ balam hastyaśvarathasaṃbādhaṃ kiṅkiṇīśatanāditam
english: The great-souled monkeys too beheld the rākṣasa army — dense with elephants, horses, and chariots, resounding with hundreds of bells.

sanskrit: nīlajīmūtasaṃkāśaṃ samudyatamahāyudham dīptānalaraviprakhyair nairṛtaiḥ sarvato vṛtam
english: Resembling blue storm-clouds, with great weapons raised, surrounded on all sides by rākṣasas blazing like fire and sun.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā balam āyāntaṃ labdhalakṣyāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ samudyatamahāśailāḥ saṃpraṇedur muhur muhuḥ
english: Seeing that army coming, the monkeys, their goal attained, with great boulders raised aloft, shouted again and again.

sanskrit: tataḥ samudghuṣṭaravaṃ niśamya rakṣogaṇā vānarayūthapānām amṛṣyamāṇāḥ paraharṣam ugraṃ mahābalā bhīmataraṃ vineduḥ
english: Then hearing the loud clamor of the monkey herd-leaders, the hosts of rākṣasas, unable to endure the others' joy, those mighty ones cried out yet more fiercely.

sanskrit: te rākṣasabalaṃ ghoraṃ praviśya hariyūthapāḥ vicerur udyataiḥ śailair nagāḥ śikhariṇo yathā
english: The monkey herd-leaders penetrated that dreadful rākṣasa force and ranged about with boulders raised, like peaked mountains moving.

sanskrit: ke cid ākāśam āviśya ke cid urvyāṃ plavaṃgamāḥ rakṣaḥsainyeṣu saṃkruddhāś cerur drumaśilāyudhāḥ
english: Some of the monkeys entered the sky, some ranged on the earth, moving furiously through the rākṣasa armies with trees and stones as weapons.

sanskrit: te pādapaśilāśailaiś cakrur vṛṣṭim anuttamām bāṇaughair vāryamāṇāś ca harayo bhīmavikramāḥ
english: With trees, stones, and boulders they made an unsurpassed rain of missiles; and the monkeys of terrible valor, even as they were restrained by showers of arrows,

sanskrit: siṃhanādān vineduś ca raṇe rākṣasavānarāḥ śilābhiś cūrṇayām āsur yātudhānān plavaṃgamāḥ
english: Both rākṣasas and monkeys uttered lion-roars in battle; the monkeys pulverized the rākṣasas with rocks.

sanskrit: nijaghnuḥ saṃyuge kruddhāḥ kavacābharaṇāvṛtān ke cid rathagatān vīrān gajavājigatān api
english: Enraged in battle, they struck those clothed in armor and ornaments — some heroes in chariots, some riding elephants and horses as well.

sanskrit: nijaghnuḥ sahasāplutya yātudhānān plavaṃgamāḥ śailaśṛṅganipātaiś ca muṣṭibhir vāntalocanāḥ celuḥ petuś ca neduś ca tatra rākṣasapuṃgavāḥ
english: The monkeys leapt up and swiftly smote the rākṣasas with drops of mountain peaks and with fists; their eyes rolling, the foremost rākṣasas staggered, fell, and roared there.

sanskrit: tataḥ śailaiś ca khaḍgaiś ca visṛṣṭair harirākṣasaiḥ muhūrtenāvṛtā bhūmir abhavac choṇitāplutā
english: Then in a moment the ground was covered and flooded with blood by the rocks and swords hurled by monkeys and rākṣasas.

sanskrit: vikīrṇaparvatākārai rakṣobhir arimardanaiḥ ākṣiptāḥ kṣipyamāṇāś ca bhagnaśūlāś ca vānaraiḥ
english: Hurled and being hurled by the enemy-crushing rākṣasas of mountain-like scattered bodies, and with their spears broken by the monkeys,

sanskrit: vānarān vānarair eva jagnus te rajanīcarāḥ rākṣasān rākṣasair eva jaghnus te vānarā api
english: Those night-rovers slew monkeys thinking they were monkeys; those monkeys too slew rākṣasas thinking they were rākṣasas.

sanskrit: ākṣipya ca śilās teṣāṃ nijaghnū rākṣasā harīn teṣāṃ cācchidya śastrāṇi jaghnū rakṣāṃsi vānarāḥ
english: Hurling rocks at them, the rākṣasas slew the monkeys; and seizing the weapons from them, the monkeys slew the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: nijaghnuḥ śailaśūlāstrair vibhiduś ca parasparam siṃhanādān vineduś ca raṇe vānararākṣasāḥ
english: They slew one another with boulders, spears, and weapons, piercing each other mutually; the monkeys and rākṣasas uttered lion-roars in battle.

sanskrit: chinnavarmatanutrāṇā rākṣasā vānarair hatāḥ rudhiraṃ prasrutās tatra rasasāram iva drumāḥ
english: Rākṣasas slain by monkeys, their armor and body-guards cut away, oozed blood there like trees their finest sap.

sanskrit: rathena ca rathaṃ cāpi vāraṇena ca vāraṇam hayena ca hayaṃ ke cin nijaghnur vānarā raṇe
english: Some monkeys in battle struck chariot against chariot, elephant against elephant, horse against horse.

sanskrit: kṣuraprair ardhacandraiś ca bhallaiś ca niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ rākṣasā vānarendrāṇāṃ cicchiduḥ pādapāñ śilāḥ
english: The rākṣasas with razor-edged, crescent-shaped, and broad-headed sharp arrows cut down the trees and rocks of the monkey lords.

sanskrit: vikīrṇaiḥ parvatāgraiś ca drumaiś chinnaiś ca saṃyuge hataiś ca kapirakṣobhir durgamā vasudhābhavat
english: With scattered mountain peaks, trees severed in battle, and slain monkeys and rākṣasas, the earth became impassable.

sanskrit: tasmin pravṛtte tumule vimarde prahṛṣyamāṇeṣu valī mukheṣu nipātyamāneṣu ca rākṣaseṣu maharṣayo devagaṇāś ca neduḥ
english: As that tumultuous slaughter raged, with the monkey-faced ones rejoicing and the rākṣasas being laid low, the great sages and hosts of gods cried out.

sanskrit: tato hayaṃ mārutatulyavegam āruhya śaktiṃ niśitāṃ pragṛhya narāntako vānararājasainyaṃ mahārṇavaṃ mīna ivāviveśa
english: Then Narāntaka, mounting a horse of wind-like speed and grasping a sharp lance, plunged into the army of the monkey king like a fish into a great ocean.

sanskrit: sa vānarān saptaśatāni vīraḥ prāsena dīptena vinirbibheda ekaḥ kṣaṇenendraripur mahātmā jaghāna sainyaṃ haripuṃgavānām
english: That hero, the great-souled enemy of Indra, alone with his blazing lance in a single moment pierced seven hundred monkeys and slaughtered the army of the bull-monkeys.

sanskrit: dadṛśuś ca mahātmānaṃ hayapṛṣṭhe pratiṣṭhitam carantaṃ harisainyeṣu vidyādharamaharṣayaḥ
english: The Vidyādharas and great sages beheld that great-souled one mounted on his horse, ranging through the monkey army.

sanskrit: sa tasya dadṛśe mārgo māṃsaśoṇitakardamaḥ patitaiḥ parvatākārair vānarair abhisaṃvṛtaḥ
english: His path was seen as a mire of flesh and blood, covered with fallen monkeys of mountain-like size.

sanskrit: yāvad vikramituṃ buddhiṃ cakruḥ plavagapuṃgavāḥ tāvad etān atikramya nirbibheda narāntakaḥ
english: Whenever the bull-monkeys set their minds to counter-attack, Narāntaka, surpassing them, would pierce them before they could act.

sanskrit: jvalantaṃ prāsam udyamya saṃgrāmānte narāntakaḥ dadāha harisainyāni vanānīva vibhāvasuḥ
english: Narāntaka, at the edge of the battle raising his flaming lance, scorched the monkey armies like fire scorching forests.

sanskrit: yāvad utpāṭayām āsur vṛkṣāñ śailān vanaukasaḥ tāvat prāsahatāḥ petur vajrakṛttā ivācalāḥ
english: Whenever the forest-dwellers began to uproot trees and boulders, that soon they fell, struck by his lance, like mountains cleft by a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: dikṣu sarvāsu balavān vicacāra narāntakaḥ pramṛdnan sarvato yuddhe prāvṛṭkāle yathānilaḥ
english: The powerful Narāntaka ranged in all directions, crushing on every side in battle like the wind in the monsoon season.

sanskrit: na śekur dhāvituṃ vīrā na sthātuṃ spandituṃ kutaḥ utpatantaṃ sthitaṃ yāntaṃ sarvān vivyādha vīryavān
english: The heroes could not flee, could not stand, much less stir; the valiant one pierced all — leaping, standing, and moving.

sanskrit: ekenāntakakalpena prāsenādityatejasā bhinnāni harisainyāni nipetur dharaṇītale
english: With a single lance like Death, of solar radiance, the monkey armies were cleft and fell to the earth.

sanskrit: vajraniṣpeṣasadṛśaṃ prāsasyābhinipātanam na śekur vānarāḥ soḍhuṃ te vinedur mahāsvanam
english: The monkeys could not bear the descent of his lance, which resembled the crushing blow of the thunderbolt; they cried out with great sound.

sanskrit: patatāṃ harivīrāṇāṃ rūpāṇi pracakāśire vajrabhinnāgrakūṭānāṃ śailānāṃ patatām iva
english: The forms of the falling monkey heroes blazed forth like mountains with peaks split by the thunderbolt falling.

sanskrit: ye tu pūrvaṃ mahātmānaḥ kumbhakarṇena pātitāḥ te 'svasthā vānaraśreṣṭhāḥ sugrīvam upatasthire
english: Those great-souled foremost monkeys who had previously been felled by Kumbhakarṇa, still unwell, attended upon Sugrīva.

sanskrit: viprekṣamāṇaḥ sugrīvo dadarśa harivāhinīm narāntakabhayatrastāṃ vidravantīm itas tataḥ
english: Sugrīva, surveying all around, saw the monkey army terrified by Narāntaka and fleeing this way and that.

sanskrit: vidrutāṃ vāhinīṃ dṛṣṭvā sa dadarśa narāntakam gṛhītaprāsam āyāntaṃ hayapṛṣṭhe pratiṣṭhitam
english: Seeing the army in flight, he beheld Narāntaka, lance in hand, coming mounted on his horse.

sanskrit: athovāca mahātejāḥ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ kumāram aṅgadaṃ vīraṃ śakratulyaparākramam
english: Then the greatly splendid Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, spoke to the heroic prince Aṅgada, equal in valor to Śakra.

sanskrit: gacchainaṃ rākṣasaṃ vīra yo 'sau turagam āsthitaḥ kṣobhayantaṃ haribalaṃ kṣipraṃ prāṇair viyojaya
english: "Go, hero, to that rākṣasa there who is mounted on a horse, disturbing the monkey force — quickly deprive him of his life."

sanskrit: sa bhartur vacanaṃ śrutvā niṣpapātāṅgadas tadā anīkān meghasaṃkāśān meghānīkād ivāṃśumān
english: Hearing his master's words, Aṅgada leapt out then from among the cloud-like armies like the sun from behind a bank of clouds.

sanskrit: śailasaṃghātasaṃkāśo harīṇām uttamo 'ṅgadaḥ rarājāṅgadasaṃnaddhaḥ sadhātur iva parvataḥ
english: Aṅgada, foremost of the monkeys, resembling a mass of mountains, wearing his armlets, shone like a mountain with its minerals.

sanskrit: nirāyudho mahātejāḥ kevalaṃ nakhadaṃṣṭravān narāntakam abhikramya vāliputro 'bravīd vacaḥ
english: Weaponless, greatly splendid, armed only with his nails and teeth, the son of Vālin approached Narāntaka and spoke.

sanskrit: tiṣṭha kiṃ prākṛtair ebhir haribhis tvaṃ kariṣyasi asmin vajrasamasparśe prāsaṃ kṣipa mamorasi
english: "Stand! What will you do with these ordinary monkeys? Hurl your lance on my chest — its touch is like the thunderbolt."

sanskrit: aṅgadasya vacaḥ śrutvā pracukrodha narāntakaḥ saṃdaśya daśanair oṣṭhaṃ niśvasya ca bhujaṃgavat
english: Hearing Aṅgada's words, Narāntaka became exceedingly enraged; he bit his lip with his teeth and hissed like a serpent.

sanskrit: sa prāsam āvidhya tadāṅgadāya samujjvalantaṃ sahasotsasarja sa vāliputrorasi vajrakalpe babhūva bhagno nyapatac ca bhūmau
english: He whirled his blazing lance and suddenly hurled it at Aṅgada; it struck the chest of the son of Vālin, became like a thunderbolt, shattered, and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: taṃ prāsam ālokya tadā vibhagnaṃ suparṇakṛttoragabhogakalpam talaṃ samudyamya sa vāliputras turaṃgamasyābhijaghāna mūrdhni
english: Seeing that lance shattered, resembling a serpent's coil cut by Suparṇa, the son of Vālin raised his palm and struck the crown of Narāntaka's horse.

sanskrit: nimagnapādaḥ sphuṭitākṣi tāro niṣkrāntajihvo 'calasaṃnikāśaḥ sa tasya vājī nipapāta bhūmau talaprahāreṇa vikīrṇamūrdhā
english: His hooves buried in the ground, his eyeballs burst, his tongue hanging out, that horse, mountain-like, fell to the earth at the palm-blow, its skull scattered.

sanskrit: narāntakaḥ krodhavaśaṃ jagāma hataṃ turagaṃ patitaṃ nirīkṣya sa muṣṭim udyamya mahāprabhāvo jaghāna śīrṣe yudhi vāliputram
english: Narāntaka, overcome by rage, seeing his horse slain and fallen, raised his fist and the mighty one struck the son of Vālin on the head in battle.

sanskrit: athāṅgado muṣṭivibhinnamūrdhā susrāva tīvraṃ rudhiraṃ bhṛśoṣṇam muhur vijajvāla mumoha cāpi saṃjñāṃ samāsādya visiṣmiye ca
english: Then Aṅgada, his head cleft by the fist, streamed intensely hot blood; he blazed repeatedly, fainted, and then regaining consciousness was astonished.

sanskrit: athāṅgado vajrasamānavegaṃ saṃvartya muṣṭiṃ giriśṛṅgakalpam nipātayām āsa tadā mahātmā narāntakasyorasi vāliputraḥ
english: Then Aṅgada, the great-souled son of Vālin, clenching his fist equal in speed to the thunderbolt and like a mountain peak, drove it down upon the chest of Narāntaka.

sanskrit: sa muṣṭiniṣpiṣṭavibhinnavakṣā jvālāṃ vamañ śoṇitadigdhagātraḥ narāntako bhūmitale papāta yathācalo vajranipātabhagnaḥ
english: His chest crushed and split by the fist, vomiting flame, his body smeared with blood, Narāntaka fell to the surface of the earth like a mountain broken by the descent of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: athāntarikṣe tridaśottamānāṃ vanaukasāṃ caiva mahāpraṇādaḥ babhūva tasmin nihate 'gryavīre narāntake vālisutena saṃkhye
english: Then in the sky there arose a great roar from the foremost of gods and from the forest-dwellers, as the foremost hero Narāntaka was slain in battle by the son of Vālin.

sanskrit: athāṅgado rāmamanaḥ praharṣaṇaṃ suduṣkaraṃ taṃ kṛtavān hi vikramam visiṣmiye so 'py ativīrya vikramaḥ punaś ca yuddhe sa babhūva harṣitaḥ
english: Then Aṅgada had accomplished that most difficult feat which was a delight to Rāma's heart; and he of surpassing valor was himself amazed at that act of valor, and once again became joyful in battle.
